newsitem.title: USA: Russia Eurobond steady after launch, Bradies down.
newsitem.headline: Russia Eurobond steady after launch, Bradies down.

text.p: Russia launched its first international bond since the Tsarist era on Thursday, but the emerging debt market shook off any inspiration and inched lower in lockstep with U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
Russia saw its five-year $1.0 billion Eurobond tighten slightly after pricing at 345 basis points over, but ended the day where it began, traders said.
"The way it has traded tells us ... the spread was about where it should have been," said Ingrid Iversen, debt strategist at UBS Securities.
Russia's MinFins gained with the issuance but dollar Vnesh slipped 1/8 to 79-1/8.
In the wider Brady market, prices were little affected by the inaugural issue, or the other major news Thrusday, that Mexico third quarter GDP rose 7.4 percent year-over-year.

"The Russia deal and the Mexican GDP number were the news, but everyone expected good things on both," one Brady bond trader said. "At the end of the day the only real influence on the market was the Treasury bond."
The benchmark U.S. T-bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.42 percent, while Argentine FRBs and Brazilian Cs closed unchanged at 84-3/4 and 71-5/8.
Brady traders saw the range-bound activity as providing a supportive tone, even though some investors may continue to take profits on their positions, locking in the strong performance of 1996.
"It seems like were not really breaking out of these ranges," said the chief trader at a major U.S. investment bank. "It looks like smooth sailing until year end."
"There's some money coming in, a lot of spwappign of assets, a lot of relative value trading," he added.
